transit.name: Transfort
transit.detail: City buses, including MAX bus rapid transit; currently fare-free

transit.name: FLEX
transit.detail: Regional bus operated by Transfort with stops between Fort Collins, Loveland, Berthoud, Longmont and Boulder

nameOrigin.text: The army post was named Camp Collins for William O. Collins, commander of the 11th Ohio Cavalry.

founded.text: The army moved its post to the present site after a flood damaged the first camp

timeline.text: After a flood damaged the camp, Colonel Collins approved a new site for the post in August.
The army post officially closed in March.
The county commissioners granted a petition for town government.
The Colorado Central Railroad's construction train arrived at the depot grounds.

sites.name: Fort Collins Museum of Discovery
sites.hours: Tuesday–Sunday 9 am–5 pm; closed Mondays and most major holidays
sites.cost: $15.50 adults; $12.75 youth 2–18, students and seniors; free under 2

trails.name: Horsetooth Mountain Open Space
trails.size: 2,711 acres between 5,430 and 7,255 feet, with 29 miles of hiking, biking and horse trails; the Horsetooth Rock Loop is five miles
trails.trailhead: The main trailhead, west of Horsetooth Reservoir and 4 miles from Fort Collins, where the walks to Horsetooth Rock and Horsetooth Falls start; also the Soderberg Trailhead
trails.season: The main trailhead is open 4 am to 11 pm, the Soderberg Trailhead sunrise to sunset. The lot fills on weekends and holidays; the County says to arrive before 9 am or after 3 pm.
trails.dogs: On a leash at all times.
trails.fee: A $10 daily entrance permit per vehicle, bought at the pay station, or an annual pass.

trails.name: Horsetooth Reservoir
trails.size: Six and a half miles of water with 1,900 acres of public land around it, and more than 150 campsites and five camper cabins
trails.address: Horsetooth Area Information Center, 4200 W. County Road 38E
trails.season: Open all year. The swim beaches open Memorial Day weekend to October 1. The information center is open weekdays 9 to 4 from November to February. The County says the ice is never safe for fishing.
trails.dogs: On a leash no longer than 10 feet.
trails.fee: An entrance permit for every vehicle: $10 a day, or $20 with a boat trailer; annual permits are $100 for county residents and $130 for others.

trails.name: Lory State Park
trails.length: 28.1 miles of trail for hiking, mountain biking and horseback riding, generally no steeper than 12 percent
trails.address: 708 Lodgepole Drive, Bellvue: about 1.6 miles up Lodgepole Drive (County Road 25G), on the left
trails.season: Open daily, 5 am to sunset; the visitor center at the north end keeps 8:30 to 4 as staffing allows. Trails close regularly for mud, and closures are posted on COTREX.
trails.dogs: On a leash and under control at all times.
trails.fee: A daily vehicle pass, $10 to $12 with Colorado plates or $15 to $17 out of state; $4 a person on foot, bike or horse.

trails.name: Pineridge Natural Area
trails.manager: City of Fort Collins Natural Areas
trails.length: Seven miles of natural-surface trail on the first ridge west of town, including the loop round Dixon Reservoir and the south end of the 9.6-mile Foothills Trail

trails.name: Cathy Fromme Prairie Natural Area
trails.manager: City of Fort Collins Natural Areas
trails.length: The paved Fossil Creek Trail runs 2.4 miles one way across the prairie, Shields Street to Luther Lane; a raptor observatory is near the Shields Street entrance
trails.season: Open daily, 5 am to 11 pm. Winter is the time to watch hawks and eagles from the raptor observatory.
trails.dogs: On a leash: horned lizards, ground-nesting songbirds and rattlesnakes live here.

trails.name: Gateway Natural Area
trails.manager: City of Fort Collins Natural Areas
trails.length: Two short trails: the Overlook Trail, 0.3 mile, and the Black Powder Trail, 0.8 mile; Seaman Reservoir is a mile farther along a flat dirt road
trails.address: 5216 Poudre Canyon Road, Bellvue, off Highway 14 where the North Fork meets the Poudre
trails.fee: $8 a day per passenger vehicle; groups of 15 or more need a special use permit.
